Article Title: Amazon adds 150 delivery stations across 118 cities to speed festive deliveries
Article Text: Amazon has unveiled its largest operations network expansion to date, launching 20 new fulfillment centres (FCs), including first-ever facilities in Raipur, Ranchi, and Varanasi. This expansion increases Amazon’s total storage capacity by 50% to 64 million cubic feet, equivalent to more than 720 Olympic-sized swimming pools. Seven of the new FCs are located in non-metro cities, strengthening Amazon’s reach into Tier 2 and Tier 3 regions.The company is also opening six new sort centres in Chikkaballapur, Hassan, Meerut, Ramanagar, Raipur, and Varanasi, expanding total sortation area by 25% from 2.4 million to 3 million square feet.Amazon has added 150 new last-mile delivery stations across 118 cities, including its first-ever presence in 12 new cities such as Bhojpur, Bokajan, Jalaun, Jehanabad, Namsai, Puruliya, Ribhoi, Senapati, Sivasagar, Udalguri, Ukhrul, and Wokha. This expansion enables faster and more reliable deliveries, with same-day services now reaching 30% more cities compared to last year.The expansion is part of Amazon’s ₹2,800 crore investment to strengthen its India operations network.Ahead of the festive season, the company will create 160,000 seasonal work opportunities across 400 cities, spanning metros and Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations.Amazon continues to scale Amazon Now, its ultra-fast delivery service, currently available in over 55 cities through more than 750 stores. The company plans to expand this “delivery in minutes” network to over 300 cities.Abhinav Singh, VP – Operations, India, APAC, Middle East, Türkiye and Africa, said: “We are investing over ₹2,800 crore to strengthen and upgrade our operations network and enhance the technology that powers our infrastructure. Ahead of the festive season, we are excited to have these new facilities operational and ready to serve customers across India.”
Article Summary: Amazon has unveiled its largest operations network expansion to date, launching 20 new fulfillment centres. This expansion increases Amazon’s total storage capacity by 50% to 64 million cubic feet, equivalent to more than 720 Olympic- sized swimming pools. Amazon has added 150 new last-mile delivery stations across 118 cities, including its first-ever presence in 12 new cities.

Article Title: Sam Altman to everyone saying China will beat US after he agreed with Dario Amodei's view that AI could kill all of us; says: We do not mean stopping, but that it should ...
Article Text:
Sam Altman

Read OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s complete post here

The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence.

Consistent rules to manage frontier risk so that we can maximize the benefits are a good idea (and we are excited by ideas like independent auditors).

Years ago, companies like ours developed things like Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks. Those were good for that moment, and focused primarily on the deployment of completed models, not what happens during their development process.

Today's shift to focusing on safe development and evaluation will need new tools.

For example, at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability, in addition to the safety work we have long done in advance of model releases.

We hope that other companies will learn from our approaches and propose their own; we think shared standards for misalignment, monitoring, and safety will lead to better outcomes.

We look forward to collaborating with our colleagues across the industry to formulate the best version of these.

When we talk about “pacing”, we do not mean “stopping”. Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs.

Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring.

Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.
Article Summary: The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, says OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot, he says.

Article Title: Microsoft donated 22.5 acres of Atlanta land in 2025; 10 months later, the city is beginning the next phase to turn it into community-focused development tied to a 20,000-home goal
Article Text:
Microsoft donated the Atlanta land in November 2025

Microsoft donated the Atlanta land in November 2025

What will happen to the 22.5-acre property

How is the Microsoft's donation linked to Atlanta's 20,000-home goal

Microsoft says the project is about families and students

Microsoft donated about 22.5 acres of land in Atlanta in November 2025. It is tied to Mayor Andre Dickens’ wider goal of constructing or preserving 20,000 affordable housing units across Atlanta by 2029. The city is now moving into the next phase of plans for the property located at Quarry Yards in the Grove Park neighborhood. The City of Atlanta and Atlanta Urban Development Corporation (AUD) will hold a community celebration on September 12 to mark the donation and highlight the work ahead. “The community event, held on Saturday, September 12, 2026, will underscore the significance of the November 2025 land donation and highlight the next phase of work to create community-focused development and expanded opportunities for Grove Park residents,” reads a release from the Mayor’s office, City of Atlanta.Microsoft purchased the Quarry Yards property in 2021 and had committed to reserving about one-quarter of the property for community use. The approximately 22.5-acre parcel was donated to the City of Atlanta in November 2025 through AUD fronts Donald Lee Hollowell Parkway in Grove Park. The city says its location could help connect residents with nearby community resources, including KIPP Woodson Academy and the Grove Park Recreation Center.The donation is part of a partnership between Microsoft, the City of Atlanta and AUD to turn the property toward uses that can benefit the surrounding community.“This land donation creates an important opportunity to deliver meaningful benefits for Grove Park residents,” Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens said.The city says the next phase will focus on creating community-focused development and expanding opportunities for Grove Park residents. The plans are also expected to support affordable housing, stronger neighborhood resources and other long-term opportunities for the community.The September 12 event will give residents and community stakeholders a chance to learn more about the next phase of work. It will also celebrate Grove Park's history and the generations of residents who have called the neighborhood home.The land donation supports Mayor Dickens’ goal of constructing or preserving 20,000 affordable housing units across Atlanta by 2029. The city says the donation will help advance that goal by making publicly controlled land available for development.AUD's mission is to use publicly controlled land to create mixed-income communities with amenities and long-term affordability. The organization is working with the city and Microsoft on the future use of the Quarry Yards parcel. “This land donation also aims to help advance Mayor Dickens’ goal of constructing or preserving 20,000 affordable housing units by 2029,” according to the mayor's office release.That makes the 22.5-acre site part of a much larger housing effort rather than a standalone land donation.Microsoft said the donation reflects a shared effort to strengthen the local community. “Through this land donation, we’re advancing a shared vision for Atlanta that supports families, empowers students, and strengthens local communities,” said Kia Floyd, General Manager of State Government Affairs for Microsoft.“We’re honored to partner with the City and AUD to make this a reality.”
Article Summary: Microsoft donated about 22.5 acres of land in Atlanta in November 2025. It is tied to Mayor Andre Dickens’ wider goal of constructing or preserving 20,000 affordable housing units across Atlanta by 2029. The city is now moving into the next phase of plans for the property located at Quarry Yards in the Grove Park neighborhood.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella agrees on slowing AI development, but also has 'wake-up message' for Dario Amodei and Sam Altman; says: For every company it is important that ...
Article Text:
Read Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella’s complete post here

Any pursuit of superintelligence has to be grounded in the core principle that if the AI we build is not helping humanity and under human control, it's not worth pursuing.

We also need to accelerate and spread the benefits of AI, such that they are diffused broadly across countries, communities, and companies.

This requires a frontier ecosystem in which both closed and open-source models can thrive.

And for firms, it’s imperative that they retain full control over their unique and tacit knowledge. Every organization should be able to build its own continuous learning loop/hill climbing machine, without becoming dependent on any one model provider, and have the ability to embed its own knowledge into models and weights they control.

So, in this context, we welcome the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right as the design goal. We also welcome ideas like "embedded evaluators" and the broader efforts to develop the mechanisms to make this more than just talk.

The key is that this cannot be controlled by a handful of entities, but must have broad representation across the ecosystem, countries, and fields, including academia.

This is the approach we are taking: broad access and choice at every layer of the AI stack; enterprise control of learning loops and models; and the “Code of Conduct” that underlies our own first party MAI models that we’ll publish tomorrow for public consultation.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has weighed in on the debate around slowing AI development, agreeing with the need for deliberate pacing but also issuing a wake-up call to industry leaders including Dario Amodei and Sam Altman . In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Nadella stressed that any pursuit of superintelligence must be grounded in the principle that AI should hep humanity and also remain under human control. Nadella further added that the benefits of AI must be accelerated and spread broadly across countries, communities and companies. He also stressed on the importance of a frontier ecosystem where both closed and open-source models can thrive making sure that innovation is also not concentrated in the hands of a few entities.Highlighting the need for organizations to retain control over their unique knowledge, Nadella noted: “Every organization should be able to build its own continuous learning loop… without becoming dependent on any one model provider.” He argued that firms must have the ability to embed their own knowledge into models and weights they control. Nadella welcomed research and deliberate pacing to get alignment right as a design goal. He also supported ideas like “embedded evaluators” and broader mechanisms to ensure AI safety is more than just talk.He cautioned against AI being controlled by a handful of entities, calling for broad representation across countries, academia, and industries.Nadella said Microsoft’s approach is to provide broad access and choice at every layer of the AI stack, enterprise control of learning loops and models, and a “Code of Conduct” for its MAI models, which will be published for public consultation.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has weighed in on the debate around slowing AI development. He agreed with the need for deliberate pacing but also issued a wake-up call to industry leaders including Dario Amodei and Sam Altman. He stressed on the importance of a frontier ecosystem where both closed and open- source models can thrive.

iPhone 18 Pro is the first iPhone with a variable aperture camera

iPhone 18 Pro Max battery lasts up to 43 hours of video playback in India

A smaller Dynamic Island shows three Live Activities at once

Siri AI arrives on iPhone 18 Pro with iOS 27

Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the most significant change sits inside the main camera. For the first time on an iPhone, the 48MP Fusion Main camera gets a variable aperture that physically controls how much light reaches the sensor. The new Pro models also get the 2nm A20 Pro chip, a larger vapour chamber, longer battery life, a smaller Dynamic Island and Siri AI, Apple's all-new assistant that arrives with iOS 27.The upgrades come at a higher price in India. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900 and the iPhone 18 Pro Max at Rs 1,79,900, both Rs 30,000 more than the starting prices of last year's iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max. Storage still begins at 256GB, and the smaller Pro now gets a 2TB option too. Here are nine biggest features you need to know before you pre-order one tomorrow or even ordering one on September 18.iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in four storage variants, starting at 256GB. Here is what each one costs in India.Six laser-cut blades move the main camera between four apertures: f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8 and f/4.0. The camera switches automatically based on light and depth of field, or users can pick a setting themselves.At f/1.48, Apple claims around 50% better low-light performance and quicker Night mode shots. At f/4.0, more of the frame stays sharp, which helps with group photos. A new sensor sits behind the lens, and developers get an API to control the aperture in their own apps.Pro controls lets users customise the Camera app by pinning their most-used settings to the top. They can manually adjust aperture, shutter speed and white balance, with a histogram to check exposure. Photographic Styles 3 adds texture and grain controls to soften skin detail or add a film look, and these edits can be reversed later. The other rear cameras are 48MP too: a 13mm Ultra Wide and a Telephoto with 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom.In the new Reference mode, the main camera's sensor signs the pixel data as the photo is taken. Apple's Private Cloud Compute then develops it into a reference image that cannot be altered. This sits next to the regular photo in the Photos app, so users can compare the two and spot edits. The feature is opt-in and will not be available in China at launch. Apple also plans to add support for Google's SynthID standard, which identifies AI-generated or AI-edited images, later this year.Cinematic mode effects, which blur the background, can now be applied to regular videos after recording, including clips shot at up to 60fps. Time-lapse mode now records in 4K with Dolby Vision HDR, and Audio Mix can separate music from background noise. For filmmakers, both phones support 4K 120fps Dolby Vision recording, ProRes RAW, Apple Log 2 and genlock for syncing multiple cameras.Built on a 2-nanometre process, the A20 Pro uses a 6-core CPU with two super cores and four efficiency cores. Its 7-core GPU is up to 40% faster than the A19 Pro's, according to Apple. The Dual 16-core Neural Engine has 32 cores in total, giving the chip twice the AI compute of last year's model, and memory bandwidth is up 50%. Both phones also get Apple's C2 modem, which the company says improves cellular reliability while using 15% less energy.Apple has borrowed from its M-series Mac chips for the A20 Pro's packaging. The silicon die now sits beside the memory, which takes the memory out of the heat path and lets the chip attach directly to the vapour chamber. The chamber has three times the surface area of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro and uses new materials. Apple claims up to 40% better sustained performance, so demanding games and larger on-device AI models can run for longer.The Indian iPhone 18 Pro Max gets up to 43 hours of video playback and up to 29 hours of typical use on a charge, according to Apple. The iPhone 18 Pro gets up to 34 hours of video playback. eSIM-only models sold in the US and some other markets get two extra hours. Wired charging reaches 50% in around 15 minutes on both phones, but only with a 60W adapter that supports Adjustable Voltage Supply, sold separately.New display technology lets Apple shrink the Dynamic Island while keeping Face ID inside it, and it can now show three Live Activities together. The displays stay at 6.3 and 6.9 inches, with ProMotion up to 120Hz. Both phones use an aluminium unibody with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and an IP68 rating. The Pro weighs 211g and the Pro Max 249g. Apple's EU repairability filing rates both class C, with a score of 3.14 against 3.04 for the iPhone 17 Pro models.iOS 27 rolls out on September 14, bringing Siri AI in beta. The new assistant can find information across messages, emails and photos, take action on what is on screen, and answer questions using online information. It can also draft text in the user's own writing style in Messages and Mail, while a Siri mode in the Camera app answers questions about what is in front of the lens. Siri AI starts in English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish coming in October.Features that run on Apple's servers, including Siri AI, come with daily usage limits, and Apple says expanded access will cost extra in the future.
Article Summary: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in four storage variants, starting at 256GB. The new Pro models also get the 2nm A20 Pro chip, a larger vapour chamber, longer battery life, a smaller Dynamic Island and Siri AI, Apple's all- new assistant that arrives with iOS 27.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sam Altman: “AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but…” - strange reality of AI risk and business opportunity
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Sam Altman

“AI will probably most likely lead to the end of the world, but in the meantime, there'll be great companies.”

What does Sam Altman’s quote mean

Opportunities and risks behind the AI boom

What can be learned from the quote

New technology can create opportunity and uncertainty at the same time

Commercial success does not settle questions about safety

Powerful technologies require more than business thinking

Short-term gains can coexist with long-term concerns

The people building a technology can still recognise its risks

What the quote means for AI now

How to apply Sam Altman’s quote in your daily life

Look at both sides of a new opportunity. Before adopting a new app, tool or technology, consider what it can improve and what problems it might introduce.

Use technology without depending on it completely. AI can help with research, writing, planning and routine tasks, but important information should still be checked independently.

Think beyond immediate benefits. Saving time or money today may be useful, but it is worth considering how a decision could affect you later.

Separate success from safety. Something becoming popular or profitable does not automatically make it reliable or risk-free.

Stay adaptable. When technology changes the way work is done, learning how to use it can be more practical than simply resisting the change.

Question impressive claims. New technology can attract excitement and investment very quickly. Checking evidence before accepting claims helps avoid unnecessary risks.

Consider consequences for other people. A decision that is efficient for one person or business may create difficulties for employees, customers or the wider community.

Keep uncertainty in mind. Not every future consequence can be predicted. Recognising that uncertainty can lead to more careful decisions.

Artificial intelligence is being developed as a tool for productivity, research and business, yet the same technology has also prompted questions about risks that could extend far beyond the companies building it. OpenA CEO Sam Altman has spoken openly about this uneasy contrast. His comments capture a peculiar feature of the current AI boom: enormous commercial possibilities are emerging alongside concerns about where increasingly powerful systems could eventually lead. Rather than presenting these as separate conversations, Altman placed them together in one striking sentence, linking the possibility of serious consequences with the creation of successful companies along the way.The quote brings together two very different ideas. Altman is suggesting that artificial intelligence could eventually create risks on a scale far beyond an ordinary technological disruption. At the same time, he recognises that the period leading up to any such outcome could produce companies of extraordinary size and influence.The phrase “in the meantime” is doing much of the work. It points to the immediate commercial reality of AI rather than treating the technology only as a distant question about humanity’s future. Businesses are already being built around artificial intelligence, while established companies are incorporating AI into software, research, customer services, manufacturing and other areas.The comment therefore reflects a tension at the heart of the AI industry. The same technology can be viewed as a source of economic growth and as something that requires serious consideration of its potential risks.Technology has often created businesses that would have been difficult to imagine before the underlying innovation arrived. The internet produced search engines, online marketplaces, social networks and cloud-computing companies. Smartphones changed the economics of communication, advertising, transport and entertainment.AI is following a similar commercial pattern, although its potential applications are unusually broad. Companies can use models to generate text and images, analyse information, write software, assist researchers, automate routine work or provide specialised services. That has created opportunities for both established technology firms and smaller companies building products around AI capabilities.Altman’s wording is unusual because he does not separate this economic opportunity from the possibility of serious harm. The two ideas appear in the same sentence. That makes the quote less about predicting a particular future and more about acknowledging the strange position of the technology: businesses may flourish while society is still working out how powerful AI should become and how it should be controlled.A technology does not have to be entirely beneficial or entirely harmful. AI can create useful products while also introducing problems that businesses, governments and researchers have to address.A company can become successful without proving that every long-term consequence of its technology is understood. Financial performance and technological safety are different questions.AI development involves engineering and investment, but it also raises questions involving law, security, education, employment and public policy.The phrase “in the meantime” highlights how quickly commercial opportunities can emerge while broader consequences remain uncertain.Acknowledging potential danger does not necessarily mean rejecting the technology itself. Altman’s quote illustrates that distinction quite clearly.Artificial intelligence is no longer confined to research laboratories. Generative AI tools are being used for writing, coding, design, customer support, research and administrative work. Companies are also investing heavily in the infrastructure needed to train and operate increasingly capable models.That commercial expansion has made AI a significant business story in its own right. New firms are being created around specialised applications, while large technology companies are competing to develop their own models and AI services.At the same time, concerns surrounding the technology have become broader. Questions about inaccurate outputs, privacy, copyright, cybersecurity, employment and the misuse of AI have moved into mainstream discussions. More speculative concerns about highly advanced AI remain part of the debate as well.Altman’s quote fits into that wider picture because it does not treat economic growth and technological risk as mutually exclusive. Both can develop together.The quote can be applied to ordinary decisions by learning to look at both the opportunity and the risk involved. AI is a useful example, but the principle extends beyond technology.
Article Summary: OpenA CEO Sam Altman has spoken openly about this uneasy contrast. His comments capture a peculiar feature of the current AI boom. Businesses are already being built around artificial intelligence, while established companies are incorporating AI into software, research, customer services, manufacturing and other areas.

Article Title: Unlocking AI's True Value: The Importance of Tokenomics in Driving ROI
Article Text:
AI behaves like an economy

What leaders can do now

How the advantage is won

By Manish Sharma, chief strategy and services officer, Accenture and Lan Guan, Chief AI and Data Officer, Accenture

Today, AI spends on the cost line of the P&L—infrastructure, inference, licensing—and it is tallied and reviewed like any other technology bill. What rarely lands is on the other side: measuring the ROI from AI.Closing this gap is the defining challenge of enterprise AI today, and most companies haven't mastered the tokenomics discipline: tying what AI consumes to the value it gives back.Tokens are the units of data a model reads and writes, and everything you ask AI to do burns through them. They began as a line on an invoice, but now they are a genuine factor of production, an input to be tracked and managed like any other.The urgency is hard to overstate. Goldman Sachs reports AI-related spending is tracking to exceed $800 billion in 2026, with token consumption likely to reach 120 quadrillion tokens a month by 2030, 24 times today's volume.So the real question for executives watching invoices climb is not how much AI costs, but how to make every dollar return more. Today, only 23% of C-suite leaders report widespread and sustained business value from AI across their organization. Businesses have to apply the same rigor to AI tokenomics as they do other technological resources.Most companies treat AI as a software expense, but it behaves like an economic system.Software costs are predictable: you buy seats, pay license fees, and the bill moves only when headcount or contracts change. AI throws that predictability out.Cost climbs with what people ask AI to do, how deeply the model thinks and how much work flows through AI. And increasingly, the heaviest users aren't people, but AI agents and automated workflows running around the clock.Cost also concentrates sharply. In nearly every deployment we've examined, including our own, fewer than 10% of users and workflows drive the majority of spending.Two enduring economic principles sum up the challenge: Jevons paradox suggests that cheaper tokens will not necessarily mean smaller AI bills. Just as more efficient steam engines expanded Britain's coal consumption rather than cutting it, cheaper inference pushes companies to run more AI, not less. Work once too expensive to justify suddenly makes financial sense. Telling employees to use less AI is not the answer; it caps the productivity gains AI exists to unlock. The smarter move is to route new demand to the cheapest model that does the job well, so the same budget buys more useful work.Meanwhile, the Pareto frontier represents the best tradeoff between cost and value. Most companies overspend where the work doesn't justify it and underinvest where advantage is genuinely at stake.Telling employees to use less AI is the wrong instinct as that caps the productivity gains it exists to deliver. The better move is to match each demand to the right model and manage consumption at the source, so the same budget buys more useful work.A handful of moves can turn AI scale into measurable return. First, the CFO and CIO should together own a single enterprise view of AI cost, usage and return. For example, a financial services firm might find that 8% of its workflows, like automated loan pre-screening, drive nearly 60% of monthly token spend, while the contact center AI actually retaining customers barely registers on the invoice. Without a unified view, the CFO cuts the wrong line.Second, embed controls into AI deployment from the start, including deciding who can use certain models and for which workstreams. By governing from day one, organizations can reduce invoice surprises.Third, draw a line in the sand that dictates which work is best for which models. Let lighter models handle tasks that break into well-defined steps and reserve the heaviest models for higher value or greater risk work, such as complex analysis or multi-step reasoning across long agent chains. Most enterprise AI usage is still search and retrieval, while a smaller group of power users demands advanced models for more complex work. Sending both workflows through the same model is how cost piles up.Fourth, measure the return, not just the cost. Consider a PowerPoint presentation that once required four finance analysts and 20 hours of work. With AI, one person can produce it in two hours at a token cost of roughly $200. The value here is the thousands of dollars of capacity freed up and redirected to higher-value work.And finally, repeat. Tokenomics is not a one-off exercise but a continuous process that must evolve as new models, tools and pricing emerge. It's closer to treasury management than an IT project.The economics of AI are being set right now. Companies are dividing into two groups: those that treat AI as a technology cost with a bill that lands each month and those that manage it as a source of measurable return.The first will spend their energy fighting compounding bills. The second will make AI's value compound faster than its cost, turning scale into durable competitive advantage. Companies that treat tokenomics as a discipline will spend the next decade ahead of the ones that wait.
Article Summary: Only 23% of C-suite leaders report widespread and sustained business value from AI. Goldman Sachs reports AI-related spending is tracking to exceed $800 billion in 2026. Most companies overspend where the work doesn't justify it and underinvest where advantage is at stake.

Article Title: World’s biggest bank to investment banking candidates: We want to know how you use AI to …
Article Text:
UBS is making AI proficiency part of its hiring process for graduates and interns

Why UBS is testing AI skills in junior bankers

​

​

How UBS is using AI internally

Other banks are also looking for AI users

How banks face a training challenge

UBS is asking prospective junior investment bankers to prove that they know how to use artificial intelligence (AI). With this move, one of the world’s largest private banks is making AI proficiency part of its hiring process for graduates and interns joining its global banking and markets divisions in 2027. The Swiss bank is among the first large financial institutions to explicitly require AI literacy for junior banking candidates.A Financial Times report cited people familiar with the matter, who said the bank wants candidates to show how they can use AI to “improve outcomes and efficiency”. The requirement will sit alongside more traditional criteria, including being on track to obtain a 2.1 undergraduate degree, and AI “fluency” questions will be added to recruitment interviews for graduate trainees and interns.The updated interview questions will focus on how candidates have used AI, not whether they know about the technology. The requirement is part of a wider shift in the skills banks are looking for as they deploy AI tools to tasks traditionally done by junior staff.This includes tasks such as financial analysis, research and preparing presentations for clients. UBS said the AI requirement would also apply to other newly advertised roles across the firm, suggesting the focus on AI capabilities is not limited to its graduate and internship programmes.UBS said: “We continuously review our recruitment criteria to ensure they reflect the skills we need. As AI is fundamentally reshaping financial services, AI capabilities and experiences have become an important aspect of future professional success and are as such relevant recruiting criteria.”Apart from hiring, UBS has also been experimenting with AI in its internal operations. The bank has created analyst avatars that can deliver video presentations to clients, freeing staff to focus on other tasks.UBS said: “AI literacy complements, rather than replaces, the academic, analytical and interpersonal skills that remain core to our approach to hiring talent.”UBS is not the only bank adding AI skills to its recruitment criteria. Spain's Santander has explicitly sought “advanced AI users” for some graduate programmes in its corporate and investment bank, according to company filings.This is happening as financial institutions use AI to automate routine processes to reduce the risk of job losses, an issue being flagged across the industry. In recent predictions made by Morgan Stanley analysts, over 200,000 jobs in the European banking sector are set to become redundant within the next five years.Some banking executives have warned that greater reliance on AI should not come at the expense of basic financial and banking knowledge. Conor Hillery, JPMorgan Chase’s co-head for Europe, Middle East and Africa, said at the FT’s global banking summit last year that lenders needed to be “very careful” that employees did not “lose an understanding of the basics and fundamentals”.JPMorgan was seeking to strike a balance between using AI to streamline simple processes and educating young employees on banking basics through core skills, Hillery opined. If technology took over responsibilities usually given to new recruits, they would have no opportunity to learn the basics through practical work.
Article Summary: UBS is among the first large financial institutions to explicitly require AI literacy for junior banking candidates. The requirement will sit alongside more traditional criteria, including being on track to obtain a 2.1 undergraduate degree. UBS said the AI requirement would also apply to other newly advertised roles across the firm.

Article Title: When Jeff Bezos told Mayor Zohran Mamdani: Villain strategy won’t work, Citadel CEO Ken Griffin is not hurting New York, in fact ...
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos is supporting the tax but rejecting the targeting

Jeff Bezos redirects the argument

Jeff Bezos criticised Zohran Mamdani’s economic policies

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for targeting Citadel CEO Ken Griffin in a viral Tax Day video promoting proposed pied-à-terre tax. Speaking with CNBC’s Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bezos said: “When you don’t know how to solve a problem, create a villain, blame them. But it won’t solve the problem. The only thing that will solve the problem is skill.” Griffin had called the video “creepy” and threatened to cancel a $6 billion Midtown development project, prompting mediation by Governor Kathy Hochul.Bezos, who owns a residence in New York City and would himself be subject to the proposed tax, did not oppose the policy itself. He called a pied-à-terre tax “a fine thing for New York to do,” likening it to hotel taxes that fall on out-of-towners. But he drew a clear line against Mamdani’s tactic of filming outside Griffin’s $238 million penthouse. “Ken Griffin isn’t a villain. He hasn’t hurt anybody. He’s not hurting New York. In fact, quite the opposite,” Bezos said.While distancing himself from the personal feud, Bezos shifted the conversation toward government inefficiency. “Any corporate CEO, CFO worth their salt—an Amazon CFO could find 3% in the federal budget on a Tuesday afternoon.There is so much waste in government spending,” he argued, suggesting fiscal discipline rather than higher taxes is the real solution.This is not the first time that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has criticised New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Recently, Bezos criticised New York City’s public school spending and Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s economic policies. He argued that increased funding alone does not solve the underlying issues. During an interview on CNBC’s Squawk Box, Bezos compared the city’s education system with Amazon’s operations, saying inefficiencies in public administration would not be tolerated in business. “If we ran Amazon the way New York City runs their school system, your packages would take six weeks to arrive. We’d have to charge you a $100 delivery fee. And then when the package did finally arrive, it’d have the wrong item in it anyway,” Bezos told CNBC.He followed up by clashing with Zohran Mamdani over billionaire taxes, arguing that raising taxes on the wealthy would not materially improve life for working-class residents. Mamdani countered: “I know a few teachers in Queens who would beg to differ.”
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos has criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for targeting Citadel CEO Ken Griffin in a viral Tax Day video. Griffin had called the video “creepy’ and threatened to cancel a $6 billion Midtown development project, prompting mediation by Governor Kathy Hochul. Bezos said: “When you don’t know how to solve a problem, create a villain, blame them.”

Article Title: As Nike stock sees worst fall in its history, tech VC Chamath Palihapitiya on what went wrong with the American shoe giant: Somewhere along the way ...
Article Text:
Nike’s historic slide

Chamath Palihapitiya on Nike’s north star

Nike recently witnessed the worst fall in its stock history, raising questions about what went wrong for the American giant once synonymous with athletic excellence. The decline prompted sharp commentary from tech venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya, who reflected on how the company lost sight of its original version. Palihapitiya argued that Nike’s early success was built on a clear North Star: “Somewhere along the way, mastery and excellence became too traditional looking. So they went to things that were just nothing to be associated with mastery or excellence. I don't aspire to be a fat person. Never have, never will. I aspire to be Michael Jordan. Always have, always will." He recalled growing up seeing icons like Michael Jordan, Tiger Woods, Serena Williams, and Pete Sampras, all representing the pinnacle of athletic achievement. “I don’t aspire to be a fat person. I aspire to be Michael Jordan,” he said, underscoring Nike’s original appeal as a brand tied to greatness.Nike shares have fallen roughly 78% from their November 2021 peak, a slide that market strategist Charlie Bilello has called the largest drawdown in the company's history as a publicly traded business — a notable distinction given that Nike has previously weathered recessions, boycotts, and supply chain disruptions without this level of sustained decline.The stock recently touched its lowest level in 12 years, erasing more than $200 billion in market value along the way.The pressure has shown up inside the company as well. According to Bloomberg reporting, CEO Elliott Hill told staff in an internal meeting earlier this year that he was worn out from constantly discussing how to fix the business, while stressing that employees couldn't simply assume everything was fine. Nike has been navigating a difficult stretch marked by shifting consumer preferences, intensifying competition from newer brands, supply chain adjustments, and a broader pivot toward direct-to-consumer sales — with sales in China falling for eight consecutive quarters and market share slipping to rivals like Hoka and On.Speaking about the decline, Palihapitiya argued that Nike's core problem traces back to losing sight of a clear guiding identity. He said that after nearly three decades in business, he's come to believe that having a clear North Star and sticking to it is essential — and that Nike's North Star, as he understood it growing up, was mastery and excellence expressed through athletics. He pointed to watching athletes like Michael Jordan, Tiger Woods, Serena Williams, and Pete Sampras as embodiments of that idea.At some point, Palihapitiya argued, that pursuit of mastery and excellence started to feel too conventional to the company, and Nike shifted toward messaging that had little connection to those qualities at all. He was blunt about his own take on that shift, saying plainly that his aspiration has always been to be like Michael Jordan, not to feel validated regardless of effort or achievement.He argued Nike should refocus on the idea that its role was never to make people feel good about themselves as they are, but to inspire people to improve by holding up genuinely elite athletes as the standard. Palihapitiya pointed to the sacrifice required of top athletes who dedicate their entire lives to mastering their craft, arguing Nike should embrace and take pride in that association rather than shy away from it — a positioning he believes has broad, universal appeal. He closed by reiterating that Nike's failure to stay anchored to that original identity of excellence and mastery is, in his view, at the heart of its current struggles.
Article Summary: Nike shares have fallen roughly 78% from their November 2021 peak. Tech venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya says the company lost sight of its original North Star. He argued Nike's North Star was mastery and excellence expressed through athletics.

Article Title: Billionaire David Sacks to Sam Altman and Dario Amodei's call to slowdown AI development: Stop pretending and fooling everyone, go ahead and ...
Article Text:
What Amodei wrote and Altman agreed to

Sacks say companies’ are disguising financial burden as charity

David Sacks has issued a scathing response to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei following their recent push to deliberately cool down the pace of artificial intelligence (AI) development. The billionaire tech investor dismissed the tech leaders’ public appeals for external frameworks, telling both of them to ‘cut the theater’ and halt their work voluntarily if they truly believe their experimental models present an existential threat.Amodei wrote an open call to “pace the frontier,” an argument Altman publicly endorsed on social media. He also got the support from Elon Musk, who is the CEO of xAI. Sacks noted that observers might expect him to oppose the idea, but his reaction is the opposite: go right ahead and stop.Sacks argued that as OpenAI and Anthropic hold an effective duopoly over leading-edge machine learning, dominating customer market share, computational breakthroughs, and revenue gains, they already control the industry's velocity. Both leaders regularly argue that their technological advantages are expanding through recursive self-improvement.Since they define the cutting edge, Sacks pointed out, they do not need an act of government or outside sign-off to simply stop releasing faster models.Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.Beyond regulatory tactics, Sacks rejected the notion that slowing down is a purely selfless endeavor. He argued that both the AI companies face crippling financial liabilities in civil court if their automated tools facilitate a catastrophic cyber strike. Pointing to the recent security incident involving Hugging Face, Sacks emphasised that the commercial market already penalises systems that act erratically or execute unauthorized digital maneuvers.Swapping raw computing power for dependability and consistency is simply smart business practice that delivers what paying customers demand, irrespective of whether companies choose to label it AI alignment or not.Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.Sacks concluded that if Altman and Amodei take immediate action on their own, they will build genuine goodwill for future regulatory debates.
Article Summary: Sacks says companies’ are disguising financial burden as charity. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei wrote an open call to ‘pace the frontier,’ an argument Altman endorsed on social media. Sacks noted that observers might expect him to oppose the idea, but his reaction is the opposite: go right ahead and stop.

Article Title: 'Upset' Ford responds to US transportation secretary’s letter to CEO Jim Farley; says: Your letter is factually wrong, Ford is the most American automaker, we ...
Article Text:
Here's Ford's statement in response to the letter from transportation secretary Duffy

The US transportation secretary Sean Duffy recently sent a letter to American car giant Ford asking the company to cut ties with CATL and Geely. The letter objects to the joint venture Ford is building with Geely at its plant in Valencia, Spain. Duffy wrote to Ford CEO Jim Farley on September 8, citing "profound concern". “When a company intentionally chooses to deepen operational dependencies on strategic competitors, it fails to act as the reliable partner the American public and this DOT require,” the letter said. The letter criticizes Ford's decision to continue manufacturing some Lincolns in China until 2030. It takes aim at Ford's technology licensing deal with CATL, under which the automaker is producing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries at a new plant in Michigan. "DOT remains deeply alarmed by Ford's continued reliance on licensed technology from Chinese battery manufacturer CATL at the operational BlueOval Battery Park facility in Marshall, Michigan," Duffy wrote.Ford has called the Duffy's letter “a wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines“. The company said, "While others continue to import Chinese batteries, Ford is investing to build batteries here in America.The CATL arrangement is a limited technology-licensing and services agreement, not a joint venture or foreign-owned manufacturing operation." In a statement, Ford pointed out that the White House praised the battery plant in a press release mere days ago.Secretary Duffy’s letter is a wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines at the expense of a company that has done more for American manufacturing than virtually any other in the nation’s history.Ford is the most American automaker. We produce more vehicles in the U.S., employ more hourly manufacturing workers and export more vehicles from the U.S. than any other automaker. While our crosstown rivals and foreign-based competitors increasingly rely on importing foreign-made vehicles from Japan, Mexico and Korea, Ford is doubling down on America.BlueOval Battery Park Michigan in Marshall is a Ford-owned and Ford-operated facility representing billions of dollars in investment and approximately 1,700 new American jobs. It is producing batteries in Michigan, with American workers, for Ford vehicles also built in America. While others continue to import Chinese batteries, Ford is investing to build batteries here in America. The CATL arrangement is a limited technology-licensing and services agreement, not a joint venture or foreign-owned manufacturing operation. Ford owns the plant, controls the operation and employs the workforce.In fact, the White House itself touted Ford’s Marshall project just last week in an official press release:Secretary Duffy’s letter also contains factual errors. Ford has not proposed a joint-venture framework as described in the letter.The letter’s claims regarding Lincoln are equally misguided. Ford is working productively with officials across the administration on trade, emissions standards and bringing manufacturing home, including a commitment to increase Lincoln production for U.S. customers. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick praised that decision just last month, describing it as evidence that manufacturers are “bringing their manufacturing home,” saying Ford is “going to rock us with bringing manufacturing back to America” and crediting the move with bringing “thousands and thousands of jobs back to America. ”Ford believes the United States must compete from a position of strength with American ownership, American jobs, American production and strong national-security safeguards. That is exactly what we are doing across our U.S. manufacturing footprint. Ford supports the Trump administration’s vision for advancing American innovation and manufacturing. Had Secretary Duffy reached out before issuing his letter to the press, we would have been happy to share more details about Ford’s U.S. commitment.
Article Summary: US transportation secretary Sean Duffy recently sent a letter to American car giant Ford asking the company to cut ties with CATL and Geely. Duffy wrote to Ford CEO Jim Farley on September 8, citing "profound concern" Ford has called the Duffy's letter “a wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines’

Article Title: OpenAI ‘drops’ IPO plans for 2026, hours after Dario Amodei’s letter calling for slowdown in AI development’ Sam Altman says: Right now would be…
Article Text:
Sam Altman rules out an OpenAI listing in 2026, and backs Dario Amodei's call to pace the frontier

As we have said, we're not rushing into an IPO. I actually think that, given everything happening with safety, this would be right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don't feel pressure on that. We've said for a long time we'll do it when we're ready, which is when the business is ready, when we feel ready from a kind of what the moment is like in society with this technology.

I would say not 2026. Yeah. We got a lot of stuff to do, and like meeting this moment of what is going to be required for safety and alignment, and how the industry and governments can work together.

I'm happy to be able to do that as a private company.

We do want to continue to make better models and products, and we do believe in iterative deployment. And I think we have been right that society needs to contend with these models at each level of capability, but that is different from saying we will just barrel full steam ahead. We've talked in the last couple of months about pausing runs as we get to these new level of capabilities to make more safety and alignment progress.

We will do more of that going forward. We have talked about the need for the industry to come together, and ideally, international governments to come together. I think that is also important.

Safety incidents cloud trillion-dollar market speculation

We Must Pace the Frontier: I’ve written a new essay on why the AI industry should slow down, with a three-part plan for doing so.

Anthropic is unilaterally committing to the first of these steps. We’ll provide third-party evaluators with permanent, employee-level access to our systems, so that they can verify adherence to our safety measures, report on incidents, and assess models’ alignment during training.

I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier. This has been a primary topic of discussions we've had at OpenAI in recent weeks.

Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same. We'll have more to share soon.

Article Title: SpaceX is going to court to stop Grimes County from releasing public records of its Terafab project as the company fears that ...
Article Text:
Why SpaceX wants the Terafab records kept private

What SpaceX says could cause competitive harm

SpaceX says some information involves security risks

What Terafab is and why the records matter

Elon Musk’s SpaceX is going to court to block Texas’ Grimes County from releasing public records tied to its proposed Terafab project. The company has argued that disclosure could reveal sensitive information about the project and cause the company “substantial competitive harm. ” The records include SpaceX’s tax abatement application, negotiations with the county, technical details, site information and project costs.According to a report by KBXT, SpaceX has filed a lawsuit in the 126th District Court of Travis County, naming Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and Grimes County as defendants. In its petition, the company argues that releasing the records could reveal its negotiating strategy, project costs and technical approach to competitors and other jurisdictions it may negotiate with in the future. SpaceX is also seeking a temporary restraining order and injunction to prevent the records from being released while the case is pending.The case follows public-records requests made in June by Grimes County Citizens for Responsible Development (GCCRD) and a Grimes County resident. The requests sought SpaceX’s tax abatement application in full, as well as records showing how the Terafab agreement was negotiated, including communications between SpaceX, the county and its consultants.Grimes County already released some Terafab agreement documents in June, but those records differ from the documents at the centre of the current lawsuit.The county initially argued that it could withhold the requested records under several exceptions to the Texas Public Information Act. Those included attorney-client privilege, anticipated litigation and the deliberative process privilege.In a ruling from July, Paxton’s office rejected nearly all of the county’s arguments. The attorney general’s office said the county could withhold certain attorney-client communications but ordered it to release the remaining records.This was also pointed out in the decision made by the Texas attorney general, in which he ruled that the two exceptions mentioned by the county, namely, trade secrets and damage to competition, could not be used by the county since they can only be used by the business.SpaceX has now raised those arguments itself in court. The company is asking a judge to exempt several categories of information from public disclosure.These include its complete tax abatement application, proposed terms and negotiating correspondence with Grimes County. SpaceX also wants technical and project information about Terafab’s design and development, site location and land-acquisition records, project cost and financial information, and personnel information, including direct contact details for employees and representatives.SpaceX contends that the documents contain information that constitutes trade secrets and other competitively sensitive information. SpaceX further contends that disclosure will cause it “substantial competitive harm” by releasing information that can be used by its competitors or other parties involved in future negotiations.The company is also arguing that some technical information should be protected under Texas homeland security law. That provision covers records that identify vulnerabilities of “critical infrastructure” to a terrorist attack.SpaceX has asked the Travis County court to prevent Grimes County from releasing any disputed records while the lawsuit is considered. Its request includes a temporary restraining order and a longer-term injunction.Paxton is sued in his capacity, and Grimes County is also made a defendant. The individuals who sought the documents are Marie Egyed, a representative of GCCRD, and Vanessa Burzynski.SpaceX describes Terafab in its court filing as a proposed semiconductor and AI-hardware manufacturing plant in Grimes County being developed in collaboration with Tesla. The company says its move into chip manufacturing is intended to support plans to put AI data centres in space.The dispute therefore involves not only the project's proposed tax incentives but also information about how SpaceX plans to develop the facility. GCCRD says its concern is whether residents should be able to see information about a project involving public tax incentives.“Our concern has never been about obtaining someone’s private phone number or sensitive security information,” said Marie Egyed, Director of Operations for Grimes County Citizens for Responsible Development, in a statement recently released. “The question is whether information concerning a massive economic-development project, including the application for public tax incentives and the negotiations surrounding those incentives, should be withheld from the citizens whose county is making these decisions. ”
Article Summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX is going to court to block Texas' Grimes County from releasing public records tied to its proposed Terafab project. The company has argued that disclosure could reveal sensitive information about the project and cause the company ‘substantial competitive harm’ The records include SpaceX’s tax abatement application, negotiations with the county, technical details, site information and project costs.

Article Title: Launch of Atari’s 'ET, the Extra-Terrestrial' is considered as biggest flop in video game history, leading to Atari’s 'death', but it left an 'El Paso warehouse mystery' that continues to haunt
Article Text:
Image credir: Atari Compendium

How Atari’s “E.T.” game became a huge problem

The Atari cartridge dump mystery

Archaeologists finally dug into the landfill

​

What was found beneath the New Mexico dump

The Atari cartridges became collectors’ items

Atari released E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial in 1982, and it is considered one of the worst failures in video game history. By then, Atari was experiencing financial difficulties, with falling console sales and increased competition. Unsold copies of the game were discovered in a warehouse in El Paso and were rumoured to have been disposed of in a landfill in Alamogordo, New Mexico. The landfill's location remained a mystery for many years.The mystery unfolded in 2014, when a dig at a New Mexico landfill led to the discovery of 1,382 Atari game cartridges, including games such as "E.T.", "Centipede", and "Pac-Man". The discovery confirmed the myth that some of the company's games were dumped at the landfill; it also raised questions about the landfill's size, since the digging was not extensive enough. From a failure of business, it became a mystery of the "El Paso warehouse".“E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial” was launched by Atari before Christmas in 1982, at a time when Atari was having a hard time in the market. Competing games were taking over the market, the console was no longer popular, and reviews were poor.Sales fell far below Atari’s initial projections, leaving large numbers of copies sitting unsold in the company’s El Paso warehouse.With little prospect of selling the remaining inventory, Atari eventually sent the cartridges to New Mexico for disposal.This was one aspect of the mystery of this dumping. Reports immediately following the incident said Atari dumped the games, and even Atari officials at the time referred to the dumping. However, the specific location and number of games were not known.James Heller, an Atari employee involved in disposing of the games, later provided a detailed account of what happened. In a Q&A with an Atari ephemera-based blog, Heller said that in 1983 he brought 12 truckloads containing 728,000 cartridges to a site measuring about 50 by 100 feet.After three days of dumping, Heller stated that they had laid six truckloads of concrete over the spot, as children were found scavenging for cartridge cases there. But even this much concrete was not sufficient to cover up all the games.“I would say that 95 percent of the cartridges dumped were new,” Heller said. “There were a number of different titles.”His report gave archaeologists a definitive spot to dig, but it would take years to figure out whether the legendary Atari cartridge dump really had the millions of cartridges eyewitnesses claimed.The project, in which Andrew Reinhard was one of the archaeologists, was filmed in 2014 in collaboration with Fuel Entertainment, Lightbox, and Microsoft. The filming crew was given permission to dig at the Alamogordo landfill; however, they were allowed to do so for only two days on four acres of the total 300-acre site.Although the digging area was small, they dug up to 30 feet into the trash pile and retrieved 1,382 Atari game cartridges, along with other pieces of equipment.The first discovery was a boxed copy of “E.T.” that still contained its game instructions, catalogue and a “Raiders of the Lost Ark” insert. Reinhard later described finding more games and hardware as the excavation continued, with thousands of cartridges representing dozens of titles being exposed.A sandstorm eventually halted the excavation. The trench containing the games was photographed, while thousands of recovered objects were collected for analysis and cataloguing.The excavation confirmed that “E.T.” cartridges had been buried at the site, but the discovery wasn't limited to Atari's infamous game. Archaeologists also found copies of “Centipede,” “Pac-Man” and other titles, along with additional Atari equipment.In 1983, Joe Lewandowski, who worked for the company responsible for collecting waste from the site, observed the dumping of the material. With Heller's help, he guided the filmmakers and the excavation team to the spot where the cartridges were buried.Only 1.3% of the landfill had been investigated; thus, the 1,382 cartridges found were only a fraction of what could have been found in the whole landfill.Some of the recovered cartridges eventually found their way into collections and auctions. Lewandowski said he auctioned several pieces and raised more than $100,000 for local institutions, including a library and a museum.An “E.T.” cartridge was also given by Fuel Entertainment to the Smithsonian Institution. While the game is stored at the American History Museum, it is not currently on display.Thus, this archaeological dig answered one side of the years-old controversy: Atari did indeed bury thousands of cartridges in the Alamogordo landfill, and “E.T.” cartridges were among them. However, because only a tiny fraction of the landfill was excavated, the extent of what lay underground was never determined.For a game that became associated with Atari's collapse, the buried cartridges eventually became something else—a physical record of one of the video game industry's most famous failures, and the answer to a mystery that had survived for more than 30 years.
Article Summary: Atari released E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial in 1982, but it was a huge failure. Unsold copies of the game were discovered in a warehouse in El Paso and were rumoured to have been disposed of in a landfill in Alamogordo, New Mexico. Reports immediately following the incident said Atari dumped the games, and even Atari officials at the time referred to the dumping. The landfill's location remained a mystery for many years.

Article Title: Matt Mullenweg back as Automattic CEO following 2-days of boardroom battle
Article Text:
Matt Mullenweg’s sudden ouster

Matt Mullenweg is back as the CEO of Automattic, returning to the helm of the WordPress.com parent firm two days after the company's board of directors voted to bench him. Following the incident that threw the software developer into internal chaos, Automattic released an official statement over the weekend verifying Mullenweg's complete reinstatement as head of the organisation. A company representative confirmed the development in an email to TechCrunch.“Matt Mullenweg is the chairman and CEO of Automattic, with full support of the board and if you search online you can see many top executives and Automatticians supporting him as well,” the spokesperson was quoted as saying. The reference to web backing pointed to an influx of supportive messages circulating on X, which Mullenweg had actively amplified through his personal profile.The corporate rift surfaced last week when Automattic's governing board passed a measure forcing the WordPress founder onto paid leave without publicly explaining the decision. Caught off guard by the decision, Mullenweg took directly to internal Slack channels, charging board members with plotting against him. By Wednesday, Automattic verified the executive shake-up, stating that Mullenweg was officially on leave and announcing that CFO Mark Davies had taken over as acting CEO with the full backing of directors.Rather than stepping away, Mullenweg resisted the administrative transition, the report says, adding that insiders revealed that the founder revoked administrative rights for multiple colleagues on Slack and announced to staff that past disputes had been settled and leadership remained firmly in his hands.Mary Hubbard, executive director of WordPress, shared a post on X, announcing the return.“I'm relieved and pleased to see Matt Mullenweg return as CEO of Automattic, the largest financial contributor to the WordPress project. Having WordPress's Co-founder and Project Lead at the helm gives me confidence that their support will remain strong. Matt has my support,” she said.
Article Summary: Matt Mullenweg is back as the CEO of Automattic, returning to the helm of the WordPress.com parent firm two days after the company's board of directors voted to bench him. A company representative confirmed the development in an email to TechCrunch. The corporate rift surfaced last week when the governing board passed a measure forcing the WordPress founder onto paid leave.

Article Title: Pay10 showcases interoperable payments ecosystem for global commerce at GFF 2026
Article Text: Pay10, an alternative payments provider, is participating in Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 as the Global Payments Solutions Partner. At the event, the company is showcasing its broader business proposition, an interoperable payments platform designed to connect global commerce with local payment infrastructure across India, the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Hungary.Over nine years, Pay10 has expanded its capabilities across digital and cross border payments, building a regulatory footprint that includes ten licenses across central banks and financial regulators. Pay10 has built its business around enabling consumers, merchants and businesses to access payment capabilities suited to local markets while creating stronger connectivity across borders. This approach underpins its broader purpose of making payments more accessible, connected and interoperable across markets, reflected at GFF 2026 through its proposition, “Enabling Businesses Across Borders”.The company’s regulatory footprint spans the Reserve Bank of India, Central Bank of the UAE, Central Bank of Bahrain, Bank Al Maghrib in Morocco and Magyar Nemzeti Bank in Hungary. Its authorisations include PA O, PA CB and PPI in India; SVF, RPS Category II, Open Finance and Exchange Business in the UAE; a Type 7 PSP Licence in Bahrain; a Payment Institution Licence in Morocco; and an Electronic Money Institution authorisation in Hungary.At GFF 2026, Pay10 is showcasing a multi market portfolio spanning digital wallets for B2B and B2C use cases, payment gateway and aggregation, DQR Sandbox and POS, cross border payments, pay in and payout capabilities, salary and B2B disbursements, utility bill payments and fund transfers.Across its markets, Pay10 is focused on combining global reach with local payment infrastructure to enable secure, compliant and interoperable payment experiences. In India, this approach would include working with established domestic payment rails such as UPI, operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), as Pay10 looks to build greater interoperability between local payment schemes and global commerce.
Article Summary: Pay10, an alternative payments provider, is participating in Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 as the Global Payments Solutions Partner. The company is showcasing its broader business proposition, an interoperable payments platform designed to connect global commerce with local payment infrastructure across India, the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Hungary.

Altman's viral preorder cancellation

Tesla Roadster: Years of delays and moving target dates

Tesla has signaled an October 1 showcase to finally pull back the curtain on its long-delayed, next-generation Roadster sports car. Altman shared a screenshot of an email sent directly to Tesla's customer team asking:"Hi, I’d like to cancel my reservation. Could you please refund me the $50K?" Expressing his frustration over the eight-year wait, Altman explained that he placed his initial deposit back in 2018:"I really was excited for the car! And I understand delays. But 7.5 years has felt like a long time to wait."Musk initially revealed the second-generation Roadster in November 2017. Accelerating from 0 to 100 km/h in under 2 seconds, marketed as the quickest street-legal production automobile ever engineered. It also claimed to deliver nearly 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) on a single battery charge.Musk teased in 2018 that an optional hardware tier would embed roughly ten miniature rocket thrusters into the chassis to dramatically boost cornering, acceleration, braking and potentially make the car hover.Despite an initial promise to enter volume manufacturing by 2020, the vehicle has faced continuous deferrals.Speaking on an investor call previously, Musk apologised to “long-suffering deposit holders,” acknowledging that while the Roadster represents “the cherry on the icing of the cake,” the automaker's core manufacturing capital has been funneled toward mass-market products and sustainable energy initiatives.

Article Title: Ganesh Chaturthi 2026: 5 ChatGPT Image 2.5 prompts for personalised wishes
Article Text:
Turning a real photo into an invitation

Five ways to use it

An invitation to celebrate Ganpati Puja at someone's house usually comes with a picture already forming in your head — the corner of the living room cleared out for the idol, the flowers someone spent an evening arranging just right, the small details that make every family's celebration look a little different from the next. A new feature built around OpenAI's newly launched ChatGPT Images 2.5 is aimed at helping people fold those specific, personal details into the invitations and greetings they send out this festival season.The core idea is straightforward: rather than generating a generic Ganpati Puja illustration from scratch, ChatGPT Images 2.5 can take an existing photograph — say, of a family's actual Ganpati Puja setup — and turn it into an invitation or illustrated greeting while keeping the recognizable details intact. OpenAI says the updated model is better at preserving those specifics, whether that's the idol's appearance, the arrangement of flowers, or the particular backdrop a family has put together, even as the image is restyled or reformatted into something shareable.That focus on recognizability is central to the pitch. The idea isn't to produce a beautiful but generic festive graphic, but to make sure the finished invitation or wish still looks unmistakably like a specific home and celebration, not an idol and setup that could belong to anyone.The guidance lays out five specific approaches, each suited to a different kind of message:* Turning a Ganpati Puja setup into an invitation: Using an actual photo of the home altar as the centerpiece of a portrait-format WhatsApp invitation, with the idol and decorations preserved and space added for event details.* Starting the invitation at the front door: Converting a photo of a home's entrance into a warm, hand-painted invitation, aimed at capturing the familiar feeling of arriving at that specific house.* Sending a postcard to someone far from home: Creating a gentle, watercolor-style postcard from a photo of the celebration for a family member or friend who can't make it this year, built around a personal message rather than a generic greeting.* Building a greeting entirely from words: Starting from scratch with just a person's name, preferred colors or flowers, and a personal message, styled as an understated paper-cut illustration.* Reviving an old celebration for a new greeting: Using an older photograph — perhaps from a home a family no longer lives in — as the basis for a softly illustrated keepsake card, preserving what's clearly visible in the original rather than inventing new details.
Article Summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT Images 2.5 can turn existing photos of Ganpati Puja celebrations into invitations and greetings. The idea is to preserve the specific details of the event, rather than create a generic graphic. There are five different ways to use the feature, each suited to a different kind of message.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu reacts to chilling AI voice scam: ‘Sadly, AI is …’
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu reacts to the warning

AI voice scam leaves X user confused

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has reacted to a chilling account of a suspected AI voice scam after an X (formerly Twitter) user said a caller sounded almost exactly like his wife. The scammer reportedly asked for a credit card to pay for gas, but the man quickly realised something was wrong because his wife was actually at home with him. The X user named Abomination, shared the incident on the platform, saying the voice sounded like his wife but had a “weird cadence”. He said he believed it could have been a voice deepfake or voice filter.The post caught the attention of Sridhar Vembu, who reacted to the account. “It is a good idea to come up with "verbal passwords" for close friends and family, so that we don't fall for these very convincing deep fake calls like the one mentioned below,” Vembu said adding “Sadly, AI is so advanced that we cannot tell real from fake easily anymore”.The Zoho founder's response came as concerns over AI deepfakes and voice cloning scams continue to grow.According to the post, the man received a call from someone claiming to be his wife. The caller said she had forgotten her wallet and needed a credit card to pay for gas. However, his wife was sitting at home with him at the time. The man also noted that she drives a Tesla, making the request even more suspicious.He said the caller sounded “100%” like his wife, although the voice had a slightly unusual rhythm.The man decided to continue the conversation to learn more about the scam. He said the responses came very quickly, leading him to believe that it could have been a voice filter rather than a fully AI-generated conversation.“I wish I had thought to record it,” he said.In the X post, the user urged people to warn their loved ones about the possibility of such scams. He also suggested using verbal passwords with children and family members so that a caller can be verified before money or sensitive information is shared.
Article Summary: X (formerly Twitter) user said a caller sounded almost exactly like his wife. The scammer reportedly asked for a credit card to pay for gas, but the man quickly realised something was wrong because his wife was at home with him. Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has reacted to the account.
